issue.title: Lazily mapped queries
issue.body:
Hi!

I am pretty excited about this.
AutoMapper already supports QueryableExtensions.
using Map<Dto,Entity().ProjectTo<Dto>() you can map an IQueryable<TEntity> to an IQueryable<TDto>
However as this mapping is made eager, applying any additioanl filters to the resulting IQueryable<TDto> is not possible.
I managed to create an MappingQueryProvider that does this lazily.
Please have a look at the unittest "AutoMapperSamples.EF.EffortQueryTests.Effort_FilteByMappedQuery()" to see the difference.

This lazy evaluation also allows to expose the IQueryable<TDto> in an OData enabled WebApi Controller. I made kind of a proof-of-concept in the project AutoMapperSamples.OData.
There you can see that I can run OData queries on the Dto-Type, and this Expression is then mapped by your ingeious AutoMapper to an EF-compatible query. I love that!

I know that it still is kind of a raw diamond, but I think it has a lot of potential!
Until now exposing an OData Endpoint that allows to execute the queries on the database directly always required you to not use DTOs at all and we both know this is horrible.

So what do you think!

One thing I have to mention.
In order to support OData, I had to add a small hack to AutoMappers MemberAccessQueryMapperVisitor. The reason is, that the WebApi.OData wraps all constant expressions into an internal type "System.Web.Http.OData.Query.Expressions.LinqParameterContainer+TypedLinqParameterContainer" as that improves EF query performance.
AuthMapper did not find a PropertyMap for it and threw an Exception. Do you have an idea how I/we could solve this?

Also this feature is not EF dependant. It should work with NHibernate as well. You'd just need to add another nuget package "Pathoschild.WebApi.NHibernate-OData" as WebApi.OData creates kind'a complex expressions that NHibernate cannot handle.
This is described in: https://github.com/Pathoschild/webapi.nhibernate-odata 

So what do you think?! How should I proceed? :)
